Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroDef Technologies Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing * followed by 1 on your telephone keypad. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroDef Technologies' Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Jane Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Strategy Officer; and Lisa Moreno, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Jane Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning. AeroDef Technologies delivered a solid performance in the third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense, and services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, we'll touch on updated revenue and earnings guidance for the full year, free cash flow generation and utilization, discussion of potential risks and opportunities, backlog growth both in absolute terms and percentage change, revenue by segment including commercial aerospace, defense, and services with year-over-year changes, expansion of service offerings and customer base, and R&D investment in next-generation platforms and technologies.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to transform our air dominance capabilities for future growth. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Jane. Now, let's turn to the financials. In the third quarter, we reported revenue of $26.4 billion, representing a 14% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $3.45. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $5.2 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year has been updated upward. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Our specific financial highlights include gross margin of 22.5%, operating income of $4.8 billion, and free cash flow of $1.4 billion.

Let me provide an update on our full-year 2024 guidance. We initially guided to revenue of $28.0 to $30.0 billion and adjusted diluted EPS of $12.00 to $13.00 back in February, taking a cautious stance amid ongoing supply chain headwinds, commercial aviation production ramps, and defense program timing risks. Today, we're raising that guidance across the board, driven by stronger-than-expected program execution, backlog conversion, and emerging tailwinds in both our commercial and defense portfolios.

In commercial aerospace, which is about 45% of our mix, global air traffic has surpassed pre-pandemic levels by 8% year-to-date according to IATA data. Our production lines are stabilizing at 42 jets per month, up from 38 in Q1, thanks to investments in partnerships like Spirit AeroSystems and a $250 million digital twin initiative for wing assembly that has reduced defects by 15%. Backlog is at a record $52 billion with book-to-bill at 1.3x, fueled by orders from Delta and Emirates for next-gen derivatives. Titanium pricing pressures from Russia-Ukraine disruptions are up 25% year-over-year, but our hedging caps exposure at 2% of COGS. Segment growth is now expected at 18-20%, up from prior 14-16%.

Defense systems, at 35% of revenue, have a $78 billion funded backlog for multi-year visibility. Geopolitical tensions are accelerating demand: U.S. DoD supplemental funding for Ukraine aid has unlocked $1.2 billion in additional Patriot missile interceptors and HIMARS munitions, while Indo-Pacific pivots boost F-35 Lot 15-17 production where we're the prime wing supplier. In Europe, NATO's 2% GDP pledge is materializing with Poland's $8 billion offset deal for Black Hawk UH-60M variants adding 150 units over five years. We've secured a $900 million IDIQ for hypersonic boost-glide vehicles under the Army's LRHW program, aligning with DARPA's glide breaker tech. Margins are expanding 150 basis points to 12.5-13.5% on fixed-price efficiencies and ERP modernization shaving 10% off indirect costs. Growth now at 12-14%, from 10-12%.

Space & Missiles, at 20%, benefits from U.S. Space Force's $30 billion FY24 budget, with GPS IIIF satellites hitting milestones ahead of schedule—three launches year-to-date via SpaceX Falcon Heavy. Commercial space shines with our Starliner analog for NASA's Commercial Crew Program at $2.5 billion through 2026, scaling hypersonic test beds for the Air Force's Mayhem program. Middle East volatility drove a 30% spike in short-range missile orders from Israel and Saudi Arabia under FMS. Book-to-bill at 1.5x, growth revised to 15-17% from 12-14%.

Corporate and other at 5% includes services and R&D, with $1.8 billion into NGAD digital engineering and CCA attritable drones for A2/AD environments against peers like China's J-20.

Overall, updated full-year 2024 guidance: revenue $30.0 to $32.0 billion, 12-17% growth over 2023 versus prior $28-30 billion, with $2.5 billion net upside from backlog acceleration and new awards. Adjusted diluted EPS $13.50 to $14.50, up from $12.00-$13.00, on 200 basis points margin expansion to 11.5-12.5%, offset by $300 million inflation. EBITDA margin 14.0-15.0% from our $500 million Resilient Supply Chain initiative localizing 70% of critical forgings. Free cash flow $3.2 to $3.8 billion, or 11-12% of revenue, capex at 3.5%. Fully diluted shares about 450 million.

Assumptions: stable FX with strong USD, oil at $80/barrel supporting airline capex, DoD at $850 billion. Risks like Boeing 737 quality issues or shutdowns persist, but derisked backlog gives confidence. This sets us to return 75% of FCF via $1.5 billion buybacks and 10% dividend hike to $2.40/share, funding 6-8% organic growth in 2025 amid the $2.5 trillion global defense supercycle through 2028 per SIPRI.

On free cash flow, Q3 generated $1.4 billion, year-to-date $4.2 billion—a 28% increase year-over-year, ahead of targets. Full-year now $6.0 to $6.5 billion, up from $5.1 billion in FY2023. This highlights portfolio resilience despite titanium shortages and labor inflation in hubs like Fort Worth and Huntsville.

FCF from operations minus capex: Q3 operational cash $1.8 billion from high-volume in Missiles & Fire Control and Aeronautics. Precision Strike like JASSM-ER and LRASM accelerated to 450 units, up 35% YoY on FFP contracts with Air Force and Navy, margins at 14.2%. Ukraine funding boosts HIMARS/GMLRS to 100+ units/month, Indo-Pacific for hypersonics.

Working capital added $300 million inflows: DSO to 52 days from 58 via streamlined FMS billing with Poland and Australia. Inventory turns 4.2x via AI-driven AeroSource platform, reducing excess by 12% YTD—key for F-35 lot transitions.

Capex $400 million or 2.8% of sales: $150 million DEW test beds in New Mexico for Space Force, $100 million additive for F-35 composites cutting lead times 40%.

FCF conversion 105% of adjusted EBITDA YTD, up from 92%, via 42% sustainment in Aeronautics backlog from F-35 PBL. U.S. DoD 65%, international 25% with FMS up 22% in Europe and Middle East, UAE THAAD $200 million.

Utilization: 40% shareholder returns ($450 million Q3: 2.1 million shares at $485 avg, dividend up 8% to $1.45/share, 1.8% yield), 30% debt reduction ($350 million prepaid, net leverage 1.8x), 20% strategic ($250 million: $120 million CCA prototypes with Boeing, $80 million Quantum Sensing, $50 million Space Domain Awareness), 10% pension ($100 million, $2.5 billion surplus).

Backlog $158 billion, up 8% YoY, 3.8x book-to-bill, 85% funded. FY25 benefits from F-35 TR-3, European rearmament.

Total backlog as of quarter-end $92.4 billion? Wait, our consolidated stands at $158 billion overall, but segment-wise: Defense Electronics/Platforms $51.8 billion up 10.5% or $4.9 billion on F-35 Lot 16 $2.1 billion, hypersonics $1.2 billion, NATO $800 million. Missiles $20.3 billion up 8.7% or $1.6 billion on JASSM/LRASM $900 million, rocket motors $400 million. Commercial $12.9 billion up 4% or $500 million on 737/A320 $300 million, nacelles $200 million. Space $7.4 billion up 2.8% or $200 million on NASA CLPS $450 million, NRO $300 million. U.S. 68% new bookings $4.9 billion on NDAA $886 billion, international 25% $1.8 billion AUKUS/Europe/UAE. Book-to-bill 1.3x, H2 growth 7-9%.

Revenue by segment: Commercial aerospace $13.2 billion, +28% YoY on RPKs +15%, OEM 180 units vs 135, engines +35% PW1100G at 45/month. North America 55%, APAC +40%, Europe +25%. Defense $10.1 billion +6% on F-35 $2.8 billion +12%, hypersonics $450 million, Black Hawk $1.1 billion. DoD 70% +8%, international +15% F-35/Patriot. Services $3.1 billion +11%, EBITDA margins +250bps to 28% on MRO fleet age 13.5 years, CFM56/V2500 +18%, defense +9%. EMEA +15%, APAC +12%.

Services expansion: $1.45 billion Q3 +28% YoY, 42% of revenue, margins to 32%, book-to-bill 1.4x, backlog $18.2 billion +22%. PMaaS on C-130J/KC-46 reduces events 35%, $250 million ARR, $1.2 billion USAF F-35 IDIQ. Hypersonics HAWC $450 million DARPA, space Orbital Analytics for 25% USSF LEO. Customers: 22 new, commercial 12% from 7% Delta/Emirates. APAC 18% doubled AUKUS P-8A/India MRFA, Middle East $600 million MQ-9/THAAD, Europe Eurofighter/Poland F-16 $900 million. Top 10 45% from 55%.

R&D $1.2 billion YTD +18%, 7.5% revenue, full-year $1.6 billion +22%. Air dominance 38% $456 million CCA TRL 7 'Penumbra' Mach 0.9 supercruise, digital twins -30% cycles for $20 billion competition. Hypersonics 25% $300 million 'Stiletto' TRL 6 CMC, scramjet ARRW, AUKUS/NATO. DE/autonomy 20% $240 million 300kW Vanguard HEL counter-UAS, AI swarms -60% workload B-21. Space 17% $204 million Orbital Forge PWSA 12 launches 2025, quantum comms. Horizon 2040 60% disruptors, IRAD 85% recapture +20bps.

Risks and opportunities: Backlog $142 billion up 12% YoY. Opportunities: F-35 ramp $2.5 billion annual by FY26, NATO 23 allies, Asia hypersonics $10 billion, commercial 4.7 billion passengers +9%, SAF $15 billion, space SDA Tranche 2 $8 billion backlog. R&D $1.2 billion AI twins -18% costs, DEWs 150kW. 8-10% CAGR revenue, EBITDA +150bps to 18%.

Risks: Supply chain titanium +40%, semis U.S.-China; mit dual-source 85%, inventory 165 days. Geopol/budget OCO -10-15% $500 million; 45% international. Labor turnover 8%; $250 million apprenticeships. Cyber +25%, FAA delays; zero-trust/CMMC, digital certs. Macro recession RPKs -5-7%; 65% defense-secured.

Sarah Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we have seen significant improvements in our supply chain management, allowing us to increase production rates on key programs like F-35 and hypersonics. We are also investing in automation and digital technologies, including our AeroSource platform, to improve efficiency and reduce costs by optimizing inventory turns and DSO.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. On the technology front, we're making significant strides in our next-generation propulsion systems, including geared turbofans and hypersonic scramjets, tying into our R&D on CCA and DEWs. We anticipate these advancements, like thermal management with CMCs and AI-driven autonomy, will give us a competitive edge in the years to come, positioning us strongly in NGAD and PWSA.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Elena. From a strategic perspective, we are actively evaluating potential acquisitions like a $1-2 billion radar play to complement our portfolio and expand market reach into AUKUS and European rearmament. We are also focused on developing new business models in PMaaS and space sustainment to capture emerging opportunities, such as hypersonics co-development with allies.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Instructions for queuing: press *1 to ask a question. Our first question comes from Josh Friedman with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Josh Friedman:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the backlog growth, both absolute and percentage change?

Jane Thompson:
Certainly, Josh. As Michael outlined, our total backlog has grown to $158 billion, reflecting an 8% year-over-year increase and strong quarterly expansion with 11 straight quarters of growth outpacing peers. Defense electronics added $4.9 billion to $51.8 billion on F-35 and hypersonics, missiles $1.6 billion to $20.3 billion from JASSM and GMD, commercial $500 million to $12.9 billion on OEM ramps, space $200 million to $7.4 billion via NASA and NRO. U.S. DoD anchors 68%, international record 25% from AUKUS and Europe. This 1.3x book-to-bill supports mid-teens EPS growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Hi, I'm curious about free cash flow generation and how you're utilizing it?

Michael Chen:
Emily, our Q3 $1.4 billion FCF brings YTD to $4.2 billion, +28%, guiding full-year $6.0-6.5 billion. Driven by $1.8 billion ops cash from precision strike ramps, $300 million working capital via DSO 52 days and 4.2x turns, capex discipline at 2.8%. Utilization balanced: $450 million returns with buybacks and dividend hike, $350 million deleveraging to 1.8x, $250 million strategic in CCA, quantum, space, $100 million pension. This fuels growth amid upcycle.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Larson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Larson:
Regarding the R&D investment in next-generation platforms and technologies?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Mike, we've ramped to $1.2 billion YTD, +18% to 7.5% of revenue, full-year $1.6 billion. CCA air dominance $456 million to TRL 7 with supercruise and MBSE, hypersonics $300 million 'Stiletto' scramjets for AUKUS, DE/autonomy $240 million 300kW HEL and swarms for B-21, space $204 million responsive sats with quantum PNT. Horizon 2040 prioritizes disruptors, recapturing 85% IRAD for backlog conversion.

Jane Thompson:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
